title: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti
hook: Krishna sets out to make peace himself, carrying Draupadi's words with him, and in Hastinapura he turns down a royal feast
carry: out of love, or out of need
tomorrow: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti

segments.voice: Yesterday Sanjaya pleaded for peace, and Yudhishthira asked for five villages. Your line was five villages, and let this end. Did you ask what a fair peace would look like? Day eight hundred fifteen.

Krishna decides to go to Hastinapura himself. One more try for peace, in person. Before he leaves, each of the brothers gives him a message, and several of them lean toward peace. Then Draupadi comes to him. She takes her long dark hair in her hand, the hair Duhshasana dragged her by in the dice hall, and she holds it up. When you speak of peace, she says, remember this. If my husbands won't fight, my old father will, and my sons will. Krishna promises her she'll see justice. Then he sets off. Today, the road to Hastinapura, and a dinner Krishna refuses to eat.
screen: `KRISHNA GOES HIMSELF.` → `DRAUPADI HOLDS UP HER HAIR.` → `REMEMBER THIS.`

segments.voice: Hastinapura gets ready for him. Duryodhana has rest houses built along the road and lays out a great feast. This is diplomacy as hospitality: if Krishna eats at his table, he's half won. Krishna passes the rest houses by. In the city he greets the old king, and then goes to Kunti, the Pandavas' mother, who has been living in Vidura's house all these years. She weeps and asks after her sons, one by one. Only then does Krishna go to Duryodhana's palace. He accepts his greeting, and declines the meal. Duryodhana is offended. Why won't you eat with us? Krishna's answer is short and sharp. A person eats another's food, he says, either out of love, or out of need. You feel no love for me, and I'm in no need. So he walks back to a much plainer house: the home of Vidura, the wise half-brother of the king, the one who spoke up for the Pandavas years ago in the dice hall. That's where Krishna eats, and that's where he stays. Look at what Krishna is doing before he says a word in the assembly. Draupadi's hair goes with him. He won't eat at the table of a man who means harm. He sleeps under the roof of a man who told the truth when it was dangerous. He visits the mother first. An embassy isn't only speeches. It's where you eat, and where you sleep, and whom you visit first.
screen: `DRAUPADI'S HAIR GOES WITH HIM` · `KUNTI ASKS AFTER HER SONS` · `A FEAST DECLINED` · then, large: `SUPPER AT VIDURA'S`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let your breathing settle. Krishna's answer named two honest reasons to share a table: love, or need. Bring to mind someone who has fed you, in any sense, out of love. Breathing in, remember one meal or one kindness from them. Breathing out, let yourself be grateful. Then think of someone you might feed, in any sense, this week. If you pray, you can hold both of them in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Udyoga. The getting ready, where Krishna carries Draupadi's words to Hastinapura and eats at Vidura's plain table.
Your line: out of love, or out of need. Today, notice where you choose to eat and with whom, and what that says before you speak. Day eight hundred fifteen.

howItsDone: Krishna's refusal of Duryodhana's feast and his meal at Vidura's house are retold in Hindu devotional storytelling, where Vidura's humble hospitality is remembered with affection.

fork.setup: you're Krishna, come to Hastinapura to talk peace. Duryodhana has laid out a grand feast in your honor. what do you do?
options: eat, and use the goodwill in tomorrow's talks.
decline: people share food out of love or need, and here there's neither.
eat a little and leave early.
fork.reveal: Krishna declines, says exactly that, and goes to eat at Vidura's plain house instead.

original.note: effort, getting ready; in this book Krishna's own journey to Hastinapura is part of the effort for peace.

trapdoor: what you thought: Krishna was just being rude to Duryodhana.
what it means: refusing the feast keeps him free; he won't accept hospitality meant to bind him.
what a scholar hears: before the assembly speech, the embassy speaks through places: Draupadi's hair, Vidura's roof, Kunti's room.
recall: dark, in red, with a noose
waits for a lapse, then enters Nala

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva (Bhagavat-yana), the messages given to Krishna, Draupadi's speech holding her hair, Krishna's refusal of Duryodhana's hospitality, his stay at Vidura's house and visit to Kunti

notes: Audit: 'walks to' Vidura's house changed to 'walks back', since Krishna had already visited Kunti there. Keeper: 'if Krishna eats at his table, he's half won' is an interpretive summary of Duryodhana's motive; confirm or soften.
All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Draupadi holds her hair and says her aged father and her sons, with Abhimanyu, will fight if her husbands will not; Krishna's assurance to her.
Confirm Krishna's reasoning for refusing Duryodhana's food (one eats another's food out of affection or in distress) and that he lodges and eats at Vidura's house.
Confirm the order: Krishna visits Kunti, Duryodhana's palace, then Vidura's house; the order here is simplified.
'Several of the brothers lean toward peace' summarizes the brothers' messages (Bhima's surprisingly mild one included); check fairness.
Duryodhana's rest houses along the road: confirm; cut if unsupported.
Editor: teach reordered so Krishna visits Kunti before Duryodhana's palace (as the text runs and as the closing line 'he visits the mother first' says); Krishna passing the rest houses by added.
